criteria.text: The diagnosis being treated must be one of the covered disorders (allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, allergic asthma, or atopic dermatitis due to dust mites).
criteria.source_quote: SCIT using preparations of aeroallergens can be considered reasonable and necessary in the management of the following disorders
criteria.if_missing: What condition/diagnosis is the immunotherapy being used to treat?

criteria.text: The route of administration must be subcutaneous (SCIT); sublingual immunotherapy is not covered.
criteria.if_missing: What route of administration is used for the immunotherapy?

criteria.text: Clinical relevance must be established by the presence of specific IgE to the allergen along with symptoms that correlate with exposure.
criteria.source_quote: The presence of specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) to that allergen, demonstrated either through allergen skin testing or serum tests for allergen specific IgE.
criteria.if_missing: Does documentation show the identified allergen correlates with the patient's clinical history/exposure and demonstrable IgE?

criteria.text: Absence of clinically relevant IgE makes treatment not reasonable and necessary.
criteria.if_missing: Is there documented clinically relevant specific IgE to the allergen?

criteria.text: AIT is not reasonable and necessary as first-line treatment for allergic rhinitis/conjunctivitis without prior medical treatment and/or environmental avoidance.
criteria.source_quote: First-line treatment for allergic rhinitis and allergic conjunctivitis in the absence of previous medical treatment and/or environmental avoidance
criteria.if_missing: Has the patient had prior medical treatment and/or attempted environmental avoidance before starting AIT?
criteria.short: No prior medical treatment or avoidance attempted (first-line use)

criteria.text: For allergic rhinitis/conjunctivitis/asthma patients, at least one of several listed clinical justifications (e.g., poor response to pharmacotherapy/avoidance for 28+ days, unacceptable medication side effects, avoidance of long-term pharmacotherapy, possible asthma prevention) must be present.
criteria.source_quote: At least 1 of the following: Poor response to pharmacotherapy, allergen avoidance, or both for a minimum of 28 consecutive days
criteria.if_missing: Is there documentation of poor response to pharmacotherapy/avoidance for at least 28 days, unacceptable medication side effects, desire to avoid long-term pharmacotherapy, or possible asthma prevention?

criteria.text: For moderate to severe atopic dermatitis due to dust mites, the patient must have failed medical management for a minimum of 90 days.
criteria.source_quote: For patients with moderate to severe AD due to dust mites who have failed medical management for a minimum of 90 days.
criteria.if_missing: Has the patient failed medical management for atopic dermatitis due to dust mites for at least 90 days?
criteria.short: No 90-day failed medical management documented for AD due to dust mites

criteria.text: Atopic dermatitis not due to dust mites is not reasonable and necessary for AIT.
criteria.source_quote: AD not due to dust mites
criteria.if_missing: Is the atopic dermatitis specifically due to dust mite sensitivity?
criteria.short: Atopic dermatitis not due to dust mites

criteria.text: SCIT during pregnancy is not reasonable and necessary.
Treatment for food sensitivities is not reasonable and necessary.
criteria.if_missing: Is the treatment intended for a food hypersensitivity/allergy?

criteria.text: Antigens must be prepared by a physician who is a Doctor of Medicine or Osteopathy.
criteria.source_quote: The antigens are prepared by a physician who is a Doctor of Medicine or Osteopathy
criteria.if_missing: Is the provider preparing the antigens a licensed MD or DO?

criteria.text: The physician who prepared the antigens must have examined the patient and determined a plan of treatment and dosage regimen.
criteria.source_quote: The physician who prepared the antigens has examined the patient and has determined a plan of treatment and a dosage regimen
criteria.if_missing: Did the physician who prepared the antigens examine the patient and establish a treatment plan and dosage regimen?
criteria.short: No documented physician exam and treatment plan

criteria.text: SCIT must be administered under the supervision of an appropriately trained physician who can recognize and treat anaphylaxis.
criteria.source_quote: SCIT should, therefore, be administered under the supervision of an appropriately trained physician who can recognize early symptoms and signs of anaphylaxis and administer emergency medications where necessary
criteria.if_missing: Is SCIT administered under supervision of a physician trained to recognize and treat anaphylaxis?
criteria.short: No appropriately trained supervising physician documented

criteria.text: SCIT must be administered only in facilities equipped to treat anaphylaxis.
criteria.source_quote: SCIT should be administered only in facilities equipped to treat anaphylaxis.
criteria.if_missing: Is the administering facility equipped to treat anaphylaxis?
criteria.short: Facility not equipped to treat anaphylaxis

criteria.text: Treatment will not be reimbursed after 2 years when there is no apparent clinical benefit.
criteria.source_quote: Treatment will not be reimbursed after a 2-year period when there is no apparent clinical benefit.
criteria.if_missing: Has the patient shown apparent clinical benefit (decreased symptoms, increased tolerance, reduced medication use) from immunotherapy?
criteria.short: No apparent clinical benefit after 2 years

new_facts.label: Is the patient currently pregnant?
new_facts.ask: Does the packet indicate the patient is currently pregnant?

new_facts.label: Is the administering facility equipped to treat anaphylaxis?
new_facts.ask: Does the packet confirm the facility administering SCIT has equipment/medications to treat anaphylaxis?

new_facts.label: Has the patient shown apparent clinical benefit from immunotherapy after 12-24 months?
new_facts.ask: Is there documentation of decreased symptoms, increased allergen tolerance, or reduced medication usage after 12-24 months of therapy?

not_modeled.quote: Some patients may not tolerate this dose due to repeated large local or systemic reactions. In this situation, the patient's highest tolerated dose becomes their maintenance dose.
not_modeled.why: Describes dose adjustment logic, not a coverage criterion to test against a single fact.

not_modeled.quote: It may be appropriate to permit patient self-administration at home for the patient with a history of life-threatening anaphylaxis who cannot receive immunotherapy in a health care facility.
not_modeled.why: Describes a case-by-case exception pathway requiring individualized clinical judgment and informed consent, not a simple testable fact.

not_modeled.quote: For those patients who have equivocal testing on IgE specific antibodies but have a strong clinical suspicion of allergic rhinitis and have a positive reaction to nasal allergen challenge, SCIT may be considered on a case-by-case basis as reasonable and necessary.
not_modeled.why: This is a discretionary case-by-case exception requiring multiple nuanced facts (equivocal IgE, strong clinical suspicion, positive nasal challenge) best left to human review rather than a strict pass/fail rule.

not_modeled.quote: Patients should be evaluated at least every 6 to 12 months while receiving immunotherapy to assess efficacy
not_modeled.why: This describes an ongoing monitoring/follow-up requirement during treatment, not a single prior-authorization gating criterion.

not_modeled.quote: There is consensus that an initial course of immunotherapy should consist of 3 to 5 years of maintenance treatment.
not_modeled.why: This is general guidance on treatment duration/consensus, not a strict coverage requirement with a clear pass/fail test.
